subject: system-design
question: Which content is typically best suited for CDN caching?
options: Per-user bank account balances
Real-time chat messages between two users
Static assets such as images, CSS, and JavaScript bundles
One-time password verification codes
explanation: Static, shareable content can be cached widely without per-user correctness risk.

subject: system-design
question: Which eviction policy removes the least recently used entry first?
options: FIFO (first in, first out)
LFU (least frequently used)
Random eviction
LRU (least recently used)
explanation: LRU assumes entries not accessed recently are less likely to be needed again.

subject: system-design
question: Which HTTP method is idempotent and typically used to replace a resource at a known URL?
options: POST
PATCH
SEND
PUT
explanation: Repeating a PUT with the same body leaves the resource in the same state; POST and PATCH are not guaranteed idempotent.

subject: system-design
question: What is a primary key?
options: A cache of the most recent queries
A copy of another table's data kept for backups
A column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table
An index that speeds up every write
explanation: Primary keys enforce uniqueness and give each row a stable identifier.

subject: system-design
question: What can a Layer 7 (application-layer) load balancer do that a Layer 4 balancer typically cannot?
options: Operate on MAC addresses inside the local network
Store database rows for faster reads
Route only UDP traffic
Route requests based on HTTP details such as the URL path or headers
explanation: Layer 7 balancers parse application protocols, so they can route by content; Layer 4 works on IP and port.

subject: system-design
question: Why does physical distance between a user and a data center affect latency?
options: Longer distances cause packets to be compressed
Signals take time to travel the distance, adding round-trip delay
Distant servers always have slower CPUs
Physical distance changes the database schema
explanation: Propagation delay is bounded by the speed of light in fiber, so distance sets a floor on round-trip time.

subject: system-design
question: What is the typical effect of batching many requests together?
options: Lower latency and lower throughput at the same time
Lower latency, but throughput drops to zero
Higher throughput, but each individual request may wait longer
No effect on either latency or throughput
explanation: Batching amortizes per-request overhead, but each request may wait for the batch to fill.

subject: system-design
question: Which HTTP status code indicates that a resource was successfully created?
options: 200 OK
201 Created
204 No Content
301 Moved Permanently
explanation: 201 signals a new resource was created, usually with a Location header; 200 is a generic success.

subject: system-design
question: What does a p99 latency of 200 ms mean?
options: The server handles 200 requests per second
The average request takes 99 ms
99% of requests complete within 200 ms
1% of requests failed with a timeout
explanation: Percentile latency describes the tail of the distribution, which often matters more than the average.

subject: system-design
question: What is a cache?
options: A log of every user action
The permanent primary copy of the data
A faster, usually smaller store kept close to where data is needed
A type of DNS record
explanation: Caches trade capacity and freshness for lower read latency and reduced load on the backing store.
